subject: Communication
title: Status and Power: Who Gets Listened To?
description: A short lesson to help you apply Status and Power: Who Gets Listened To?.

hook.text: In meetings, the highest-paid person's opinion often wins — regardless of quality.

buildup.text: We listen more attentively to people with higher status, authority, or perceived expertise — even when they're wrong.

discovery.text: Conversely, we dismiss ideas from lower-status speakers. Nurses who noticed medical errors were often ignored by doctors.

twist.text: Power also corrupts the powerful listener. High-power individuals interrupt more, listen less, and are more likely to dismiss.

climax.text: Organizations that flatten listening hierarchies — where anyone can be heard — make fewer errors and innovate faster.

punchline.text: The best ideas don't always come from the top.

quiz.question: How does power affect listening behavior?
options: High-power individuals interrupt more and listen less
Power has no effect on listening
